name: Abigail Spanberger
role: Governor of Virginia (2026–present); U.S. Representative from Virginia (2019–2025)
summary: A self-described pragmatic moderate Democrat who has centered her politics on affordability, bipartisan deal-making and public institutions. She supports abortion rights, same-sex marriage, gun restrictions, a $15 minimum wage and climate measures such as rejoining RGGI, while backing police funding, border security, right-to-work and an all-of-the-above energy mix including nuclear. She has rejected 'defund the police' and 'socialism' rhetoric and opposes private-school vouchers.

sources.title: Abigail Spanberger's plans for Virginia public schools (The 19th, Aug 2025)
sources.author: The 19th
sources.usedFor: Report on her campaign education plan: opposes private-school vouchers

universal-healthcare.rationale: Backs the Affordable Care Act, a public option (Medicare-X Choice Act) and, as governor, state premium assistance for ACA plans; no statement endorsing a state guarantee of coverage for everyone, so the agreement is limited.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Called for and signed the law raising Virginia's minimum wage from $12.77 to $15 by 2028, saying a full-time worker should be able to afford to live in Virginia.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Pushed laws to curb pharmacy benefit managers, make large energy users such as data centers bear their share of costs, and restrict non-compete agreements, while describing herself as pro-business.

cut-welfare.rationale: Criticizes federal cuts to Medicaid and healthcare and ordered a task force to protect eligible access to Medicaid and SNAP; no statement on welfare causing dependency.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No stated position on recreational drugs in general; her cannabis position is something nearby.

state-harmful.rationale: Says Virginians want a government that works and describes her mandate as delivering through state action for families, schools and businesses, which is incompatible with treating the state as unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Says she supports the Second Amendment but signed an assault-weapons and large-magazine sale ban, raised the purchase age to 21 and restored private-sale background checks; earlier voted for background checks and the 2022 assault weapons ban.

empower-police-military.rationale: Opposes defunding the police and pledges investment in police recruitment, retention and training; no statement on expanding police authority or military funding.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted for the Respect for Marriage Act twice, supports removing Virginia's marriage ban from its constitution and signed the measure sending the amendment to voters.

abortion-legal.rationale: Says she supports the Roe standard and the Virginia constitutional amendment on reproductive freedom, which she signed and will campaign for; voted for the Women's Health Protection Act.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Cited the disproportionate effect of marijuana enforcement on communities of color as an inequity to address and vetoed a bill that would have removed hundreds of women- and minority-owned firms from the state contracting program.

free-trade.rationale: Directed state agencies to help farmers and producers expand exports, said rural communities should reap the benefits of trade, and backed the USMCA while in Congress.

open-borders.rationale: Supports stronger border security and cited a bill signed by President Trump tightening border security and curbing fentanyl; opposes the border wall but has not argued for open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Frames economic growth and competitiveness as goals, warning that inaction would mean slower growth and lost talent, while also backing climate measures.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Calls climate change a major threat, is rejoining the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative and joined the US Climate Alliance; she criticized the Green New Deal as vague and also supports natural gas for near-term needs.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Called advanced nuclear extraordinarily important, supported it in Congress, and as governor listed nuclear alongside solar for Virginia's energy independence.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Criticizes current tariffs and trade wars as hurting Virginia farmers, ports and businesses and set up a task force on tariff impacts.

democracy-best.rationale: Says democracy is strongest when every eligible citizen can participate and that she trusts voters to decide on constitutional amendments; no statement about voters choosing badly.

political-violence-never.rationale: Declared that political violence has no place in Virginia, against anyone and for any reason, and denounced violent rhetoric from either side in the 2025 debate.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Said her mandate is not an ideological agenda but getting things done for families, schools and businesses, calling her proposals 'not about ideology' but 'about results'.

school-vouchers.rationale: Opposes private-school vouchers: said she does not support taking public dollars out of public schools, and her campaign plan opposed creating vouchers.

force-without-un.rationale: Reported to have supported the June 2025 US strikes on Iranian nuclear sites, which were carried out without UN Security Council authorization; no statement on the UN question itself.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said every citizen should be able to marry the person they love with their family recognized equally under the law.

death-penalty.rationale: Cosponsored the Federal Death Penalty Prohibition Act, which would bar federal executions; a cosponsorship alone shows support for that bill.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Vetoed a bill narrowing the state's small, women- and minority-owned business contracting program; this concerns contracting rather than college admissions or hiring.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Voted for the Equality Act and criticized her opponent in the debate for saying it is acceptable to fire someone for being gay, calling it discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Supports writing reproductive freedom, marriage equality and automatic restoration of voting rights into Virginia's constitution, saying the constitution should state those protections.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Her record on LGBTQ equality (Equality Act, Respect for Marriage Act, marriage amendment) is inconsistent with criminalizing same-sex relations; no direct statement on criminal bans.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Voted for the Equality Act (which covers gender identity) and as governor ended a rulemaking that would have barred transgender women from women's sports and facilities, but on school bathrooms and sports she said local communities should decide.

social-market-economy.rationale: Argues that being pro-business and pro-worker are compatible, pairing business-climate commitments with paid leave, paid sick days and a $15 minimum wage.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Told House Democrats in 2020 that Democrats should not use 'defund the police' language, which she said cost members seats, and as governor commits to funding recruitment and training of law enforcement.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Is rejoining RGGI, a regional cap-and-trade program that charges power plants for carbon emissions, and said its revenue funds flood mitigation and bill relief.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Supported extending collective bargaining to public employees in principle but vetoed the 2026 bill after amendments to phase it in were rejected; evidence points both ways.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Said on the campaign trail and again as governor that she will not repeal Virginia's right-to-work law, which bars requiring union membership or dues as a job condition; she framed it as business predictability.

notes: Most recent positions win. She became governor on January 17, 2026. Her 2020 remarks on 'defund the police' and 'socialism' came from a leaked caucus call; she said the labels hurt Democrats in swing districts. On transgender school policy she said decisions belong to local communities and avoided a direct yes or no in the 2025 debate. Positions on Israel, taxes on the wealthy, voter ID and most foreign policy statements were not found in her own words and are left null.
